bullets.title: CPI print today is the key macro catalyst; bond market pricing 63% hike probability for Sep 16
bullets.body: JPM's Feroli forecasts Headline CPI +0.38% MoM and Core +0.21% MoM. A 0.2% core read is viewed as low enough for a Fed hold and equity-positive; a 0.3%+ print could trigger hike consideration. Bond market currently prices ~63% probability of a 25bp hike at the Sep 16 FOMC, with Oct/Dec hike odds at ~27%/~54%.

bullets.title: JPMorgan macro: AI capex boom + fiscal deficits = structurally higher rates; UST target 5.5%
bullets.body: JPM's Joyce Chang flags AI capex issuance in US IG debt hit $266bn YTD 2026 vs $139bn for all of 2025, with $2.1trn projected over 5 years. US 2026 deficit running ~$170bn ahead of last year; CBO projects ~$2.1trn (~6.5% GDP). Long-term UST yield target is ~5.5% (2.5% real + ~3% inflation), with net interest costs expected to double to $2.1trn by 2035. Historical investment booms of comparable scale have never ended in soft landings.

bullets.title: Dollar at 3-month lows; commodities at cycle highs; Hedgeye exits equal-weight S&P on narrowing breadth
bullets.body: Dollar Index making fresh 3-month lows, adding incremental inflation pressure. CRB Commodities at new cycle highs; Bitcoin, Wheat, and Uranium benefiting. Hedgeye exited equal-weight S&P and broadening exposures after booking gains near overbought levels, noting breadth narrowed with 71% of stocks down avg 2.1%. SPY key pivot at 7,695: bearish trade signal, but bullish trend — upside resumes on reclaim.

bullets.title: Oil surging past $100/bbl on US-Iran military escalation; Saudi, Russia supply disruptions compound
bullets.body: Brent crude broke above $100/bbl following US-Iran escalation including vessel attacks and ballistic missiles fired at a US Navy warship. Saudi Arabia halted energy facilities after Houthi strikes on Jazan refinery; Russia refinery runs fell to 3.8M bbl/d after attacks on four major facilities. OPEC crude output declined 900k bbl/day in August to 19.91M bbl/day, with Saudi production cut by 1M bbl/day. Hormuz traffic fell to six commodity vessels amid security concerns.

bullets.title: META Muse AI agent launch: 10x compute usage vs test cohorts; Morgan Stanley calls it a 'massive unpriced call option'
bullets.body: META's Muse personal AI agent is driving 10x more compute consumption than testing cohorts, priced at $0–$100/month. Trained on 10x more compute than prior models (Watermelon vs Avocado/Spark), with post-Watermelon models already in training. Morgan Stanley views Muse as one of the largest unpriced call options in META, with stock trading ~18x 2028 EPS. KeyBanc maintains Overweight citing low learning curve, distribution breadth, and safety focus. Near-term risk: 2027 capex/opex guide could overshadow results.

bullets.title: AAPL reveals foldable iPhone Duo at $2,199 starting price; camera/battery trade-offs flagged
bullets.body: Apple announced the iPhone Duo foldable today at a starting price of $2,199 (vs. prior $1,999 target), with SKUs potentially reaching $3,000. Morgan Stanley notes trade-offs vs. conventional premium iPhones: weaker camera, shorter battery, lower durability. Hedgeye notes AAPL remains bullish trade/trend.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure demand remains robust across conferences; networking/data center supply still constrained
bullets.body: Across Citi and Goldman TMT Day 1 takeaways, AI demand impulse is described as strong with AVGO/QCOM seeing tight supply and extended lead times. ANET is seeing strong demand in AI back-end networking; CSCO reports agentic AI driving 5x increase in network bandwidth consumption. Data center build costs have broadened to $10–20M per MW, with firms holding energized power pipelines able to capture favorable leasing for the next 6–12 months. Nebius targets ~1GW capacity this year en route to 5GW total, expecting the current supply-demand imbalance to normalize in 18–24 months.

bullets.title: Semis rebounding: SOX testing $12K resistance; memory, HDDs, optical leading; quant/CTA flows key driver
bullets.body: Semiconductors are up 530bps in September with memory, HDDs, and optical stocks leading. SOX at $11.9K is testing $12K resistance. Mizuho notes buyside sentiment remained positive on semi fundamentals throughout the pullback; quant, passive, and CTA fund flows are cited as a bigger factor in the recent strength than fundamental re-ratings, with software having been overbought and semis oversold. Hedgeye previously exited DRAM short and semis short after momentum exhausted.

bullets.title: WFE demand tracking above $150B in CY26; KLAC backlog $12.6B with visibility into CY28
bullets.body: CY26 WFE is now tracking above $150B with 2H26 revenue expected ~20% above 1H26. KLAC's $12.6B backlog provides shipment visibility through CY27 and into early CY28, with optics/calcium fluoride components carrying 18–24+ month lead times. Advanced packaging revenue grew ~70% to ~$1.1B with share rising from ~2% in CY23 to 7–8% in CY26. Gross margin faces a ~100bps headwind from memory input cost inflation vs. the prior ~75bps estimate.

bullets.title: HDD supply/demand imbalance persists through FY27+; STX and WDC both see pricing power and 25%+ exabyte CAGRs
bullets.body: Both Seagate and Western Digital presented at Citi TMT with consistent messaging: nearline HDD capacity demand remains above supply, expected to persist through FY27 and beyond. STX targets at least 25% exabyte CAGR over 1–3 years with HAMR drives scaling from 30TB to 50TB+; WDC sees cloud driving ~90% of its HDD business with multi-year demand visibility into 2030–2031. Both expect pricing power and margin expansion; CapEx guided at 4–6% of revenue.

bullets.title: US consumer spending tracking 9% QTD per Visa; retail web traffic decelerated in Sept Week 1 (likely Labor Day distortion)
bullets.body: Visa's U.S. consumer spending is tracking +9% QTD through August with continued global strength despite sentiment uncertainty. Citi retail web traffic data shows Sept Week 1 average +18.2% vs +23.6% in Aug Week 4; Labor Day timing shift and warmer temps (+5.6°F vs prior year) are cited as likely distortions. HD and LOW turned negative in Sept Week 1; RH decelerated to mid-teens from low-20s.

bullets.title: Healthcare sector under structural cost pressure: No Surprises Act IDR, ACA subsidy expiry, tighter macro
bullets.body: A morning call flagged that health insurers' cost structures assumed conditions that no longer hold. The No Surprises Act IDR process will pressure premiums upward; expiring enhanced ACA subsidies will increase uncompensated care costs. Tighter monetary policy compounds the structural headwinds, and the industry's political 'blame game' is unlikely to reverse the trend.

bullets.title: VIX +4.8% to 16.48; unusual options volume surge across 25+ names; breadth narrowing
bullets.body: VIX rose 4.8% to 16.48 intraday with S&P 500 at 7,631.58 (+0.6%). Widespread unusual options activity is reported across 25+ tickers showing 200–1,700% above 30-day average volume. Hedgeye's breadth indicator shows 71% of stocks down an average of 2.1%, with healthcare (XLV) and software hit hardest on the prior session.

bullets.title: EU Affordable Housing Act would empower local authorities to restrict short-term rentals (ABNB risk)
bullets.body: The European Commission proposed an Affordable Housing Act framework allowing public authorities to restrict short-term rentals where they have demonstrably reduced long-term housing stock for at least three years. Restrictions would target commercial short-term rental activity, creating potential headwinds for Airbnb and European-exposed OTAs. Separately, the EU General Court upheld the 2023 block on Booking's acquisition of Etraveli Group, affirming antitrust concerns around hotel OTA dominance.

bullets.title: Fox-Roku merger receives DOJ Second Request; deal still expected to close H1 2027
bullets.body: Fox Corp. and Roku each received a Second Request from the DOJ on Sept 8, extending the HSR waiting period. The $160/share ($22B enterprise value) deal — $96 cash + 0.9693 FOX Class A shares per ROKU share — is still expected to close by H1 2027. Fox has $12B committed bridge financing from Morgan Stanley and targets $400M in run-rate cost synergies.

bullets.title: ORCL F1Q27 preview: Street watching GPU capacity ramp, cloud acceleration, and margin pressure
bullets.body: Street consensus for ORCL F1Q27 is $19.135B revenue, 61.9% gross margin, 40.7% operating margin, and $1.74 EPS. Management previously guided incremental capacity would 'approach 1GW' in F1Q; investors are watching for delivery and FY27 timeline updates. Cloud revenue guidance calls for +58%–64% growth with acceleration expected in 2H27, though gross margins face pressure from the OCI infrastructure ramp and $70B capex commitment.

bullets.title: Germany reaffirms fiscal/reform agenda; GDP trajectory improving toward 1.75% annualized into mid-2027
bullets.body: JPMorgan notes the CDU/CSU-SPD coalition is reaffirming its fiscal and reform commitments after initial post-election wavering. German GDP grew at almost 1.5% annualized over the past three quarters with a forecast pickup to 1.75% annualized through mid-2027. Pension reform modifications are expected to be modest, and government reform efforts are seen as a positive for business investment.

bullets.title: ADP weekly hiring data shows 12K average jobs added (4-wk ending 8/22); second consecutive weekly increase
bullets.body: ADP's survey of ~26M private workers shows an average of 12K jobs added weekly for the four weeks ending 8/22, up from 10K the prior week — the second consecutive week of acceleration. Data excludes federal workers.

bullets.title: Mortgage applications fell 2.7% as 30-year rates rose to 6.85%; housing index making lower lows
bullets.body: Mortgage applications fell 2.7% for the week ending 9/4, with 30-year rates rising to 6.85% from 6.79%. Refi volume is 41% of mix. Hedgeye notes the ITB (housing) index is making lower lows and lower highs as bond yields rise, with the 2-year yield risk range at 4.28%–4.50%.

bullets.title: AI sovereignty becoming a government priority; AI capex fragmentation creating multi-sector investment theme
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley hosted a webcast flagging AI capability as increasingly strategic for governments, with growing AI capex opportunity from government demand. The risk of broader tech restrictions and geopolitical fragmentation is creating cross-sector investment opportunities. JPMorgan's Chang separately noted that middle powers are rejecting 'winner-takes-all' narratives, optimizing for autonomy and diversification in AI and US-China competition.
